nodes.summary: There is a group $G$ satisfying the maximal condition on subgroups (there is no infinite strictly ascending chain of subgroups of $G$) that has an infinite descending chain $H_0 \ge H_1 \ge \cdots$ of subgroups in which every index $|H_i : H_{i+1}|$ is infinite. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.14(b) negatively.
nodes.title: A group with the maximal condition can fail the weak minimal condition

nodes.summary: Kourovka 10.14(b): every group with the maximal condition on subgroups satisfies the weak minimal condition on subgroups.
nodes.title: Maximal condition implies weak minimal condition

nodes.summary: There is a group $G$ satisfying the minimal condition on subgroups (there is no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups of $G$) that has an infinite ascending chain $H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots$ of subgroups in which every index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ is infinite. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.14(a) negatively.
nodes.title: A group with the minimal condition can fail the weak maximal condition

nodes.summary: Kourovka 10.14(a) (D. I. Zaitsev): every group with the minimal condition on subgroups satisfies the weak maximal condition on subgroups.
nodes.title: Minimal condition implies weak maximal condition

nodes.summary: A group $G$ satisfies the weak maximal condition on subgroups when there is no infinite ascending chain $H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots$ of subgroups of $G$ in which every index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Weak maximal condition on subgroups

nodes.summary: The weak minimal condition on subgroups: there is no infinite descending chain `H₀ ≥ H₁ ≥ ⋯` of subgroups with every index `|Hᵢ : Hᵢ₊₁|` infinite.
nodes.title: Weak minimal condition on subgroups

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
